headline: Betul 8 Capsizes Off Bulgaria, 12 Rescued
subheadline: Crew report sea drone strike; cause under investigation
insight: Somali-flag cargo ship Betul 8, carrying wheat from Tulcea to Egypt, capsized in Bulgaria's EEZ on 16 Nov. Air Force helicopters winched all 12 crew from two life rafts.

factCheck.notes: CORROBORATED: Bulgarian Ministry of Transport via BTA, Euronews, Al Jazeera, MarEx, gCaptain. Betul 8 (IMO 8817198, Somali flag) capsized in Bulgaria's EEZ on 16 Nov 2026; distress call shortly after 09:00 local; all 12 crew winched from two life rafts by Bulgarian Air Force Cougar helicopters to Chaika naval air base, Varna; one minor head injury; MRCC Varna coordinated; MCM Black Sea vessels deployed, water sampled for pollution. Sea drone cause is the crew's account only, framed as reported; no attribution. Cargo quantity conflicts between sources, so not stated. Re-searched 06:50 UTC 17 Nov: no new official findings. Event date 16 Nov shown; published next day, not presented as new today.

meta.description: The Somali-flagged general cargo ship Betul 8, carrying bulk wheat from Tulcea in Romania to Egypt, capsized in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea on 16 November 2026 after a distress call shortly after 09:00 local time. Bulgarian Air Force Cougar helicopters winched all 12 crew from two life rafts and flew them to the Chaika naval air base in Varna; one seafarer had a minor head injury. MRCC Varna coordinated the response and vessels of the Black Sea mine countermeasures task group were deployed, with a naval ship sampling the water for pollution. Crew members say two sea drones struck the ship; Bulgarian authorities say the cause will be determined after questioning the crew.
